title: Paloma and the Confession
premise: When the coffin of Vesper Hollow's beloved founder, Aldous Crane, is exhumed for a centennial ceremony, archivist Sable Ashgrove discovers it empty — and a fresh confession letter hidden in the crypt wall naming his death as murder. The town's powerful founding families close ranks, insisting the witness named in the confession died decades ago, but Sable finds evidence the witness lived on in hiding. As the trial of the accused gravedigger approaches, she races to find him while dodging threats from those who would rather the past stay buried. In the end, the witness — the founder's own disinherited daughter, alive and old — testifies, justice lands outside the law's original target, and Sable chooses her found family among the town's outcasts over the institution that raised her.
about_author: Orsen Winterbourne is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing births, deaths, and the silences between them. They write mysteries about people who keep secrets for good reasons and towns that keep them for bad ones.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Sable Ashgrove catalogs the cathedral crypt before the founder's centennial exhumation, establishing her solitary life among records and her quiet bond with the verger, Tam. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: An Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: During the public exhumation, the coffin lid opens on nothing but century-old air. The crowd panics; the mayor demands discretion. Sable notices the coffin was sealed from the inside. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: shock curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: What the Wall Keeps
chapters.summary: Searching crypt records for an explanation, Sable pries loose a loose mortar stone and finds a confession letter: 'I did not kill him, but I know who did.' It names a witness — Mirabel Crane, the founder's daughter, dead these sixty years. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread mixed with purpose.

chapters.title: The Gravedigger's Boy
chapters.summary: Police arrest Eli Marsh, a young gravedigger whose grandfather served the Crane household, claiming family motive. Sable believes he's a scapegoat. Tam warns her the founding families ruin anyone who digs. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: first defiance.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable cross-references burial registers and finds Mirabel Crane's death certificate signed by a doctor who never existed in the medical rolls. Someone falsified a death. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the thrill of a crack in the story.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Founders
chapters.summary: Invited to the Ashcombe estate under polite pretenses, Sable endures veiled threats from matriarch Cordelia Ashcombe, who offers her a promotion to forget the letter. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation versus conscience.

chapters.title: Tam's Silence
chapters.summary: Sable discovers Tam knew the crypt held secrets — his own grandfather helped seal it. Their friendship fractures when he begs her to stop. POV: alternating Sable and Tam. Emotional beat: betrayal and its understandable roots.

chapters.title: The House That Burned Twice
chapters.summary: Following land records, Sable visits the ruins of the Crane summer house, burned shortly after the founder's death, and finds a child's grave marker with no body beneath. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief for a girl erased twice.

chapters.title: Fire Follows Her
chapters.summary: Someone sets fire to the archive's east wing; the confession letter survives only because Sable took it home. She realizes she's no longer investigating — she's being hunted. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Eli Speaks
chapters.summary: In jail, Eli tells Sable his grandfather's dying words: 'Mirabel lives where the river forgets its name.' He asks her to save them both. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: alliance formed in desperation.

chapters.title: Where the River Forgets
chapters.summary: Sable traces the phrase to a defunct mill village and finds an elderly woman, 'Ruth Fen,' whose hands bear a Crane signet ring worn smooth. She doesn't deny who she is. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: awe and tenderness.

chapters.title: Sixty Years of Running
chapters.summary: Mirabel recounts the night her father died — she saw Cordelia Ashcombe's mother poison him, was framed as mad, and fled a staged death. The empty coffin was arranged by a sympathetic undertaker. POV: Mirabel (framed within Sable's visit). Emotional beat: catharsis long deferred.

chapters.title: Why She Won't Testify
chapters.summary: Mirabel refuses the trial: testifying means exposing the undertaker's descendants and reopening wounds for a town that abandoned her. Sable must decide whether to respect or persuade her. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: moral impasse.

chapters.title: The Trial Opens
chapters.summary: Eli's trial begins; the prosecution's case is tidy and hollow. Sable watches Cordelia in the gallery and sees fear, not confidence — the Ashcombes are nervous about something new. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: A Second Letter
chapters.summary: Cordelia privately offers Sable the archive directorship and a quiet pension if the witness stays buried. Sable realizes Cordelia knows Mirabel lives — and has known for years. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: fury crystallizing into strategy.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Sable gathers her unlikely allies — Tam, Eli's sister, the retired undertaker's granddaughter — and they plan to protect Mirabel through the trial. Each brings a piece of the record chain. POV: rotating among the group. Emotional beat: belonging forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Night Visitors
chapters.summary: Ashcombe men ransack Mirabel's cottage while she's moved to safety; Sable confronts them and is injured but photographs their faces. The law won't help her, so she builds her own case file. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: cost of the fight made flesh.

chapters.title: The Undertaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: The granddaughter produces the undertaker's private ledger proving the coffin was empty at burial — meaning the founder was never interred, and someone paid to fake it. The payment trail leads to the Ashcombes. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: What Cordelia Knows
chapters.summary: Sable confronts Cordelia with the ledger; Cordelia breaks, confessing her mother's crime was covered up by three generations of payoffs, and that she kept Mirabel's existence secret out of inherited shame. POV: dual confrontation. Emotional beat: villainy revealed as rot passed down like property.

chapters.title: The Witness Walks In
chapters.summary: At trial, as the verdict nears, Mirabel Crane enters the courtroom on Sable's arm and identifies herself. The courtroom erupts; the judge must decide what sixty years of false records mean. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: triumph laced with terror.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Eli is acquitted; the statute of limitations shields the dead poisoner, but the Ashcombe fortune collapses under fraud exposure, and Cordelia publicly surrenders the family archives to Mirabel. Justice arrives sideways, imperfectly, but it arrives. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sable reopens the crypt as a public memorial, buries the empty coffin with honors, and takes tea with Mirabel, who gives her the nickname 'Paloma' — the dove that found what was hidden. Sable finally belongs. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: peace earned, home chosen.
